title: Implement favicon.svg fallback
body:
(History and context: #4758, #6954.)

**Situation:** At the moment, the [“Link type `icon`”](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#rel-icon) section of the spec provisions that favicons fall back on a favicon.ico file in the domain root:

> Let _request_ be a new request whose URL is the URL record obtained by resolving the URL "`/favicon.ico`" against the `Document` object's URL

**Problem:** This fallback solution is _great_ because it established a standard that favicons can be left at the domain root without requiring _any_ code. However, it fails the increased demand and utility of a favicon to be a vector graphic. That is, developers cannot use this no-code-required fallback option to serve other valid use cases, notably to be able to serve different icon sizes through a format that allows to do so with one file (i.e., a vector graphic) †.

**Solution:** Keep the favicon.ico fallback, but also fall back to favicon._svg_ if favicon.ico is not available. This would be compatible with current implementations but offer greater utility (more efficiently serve more sizing needs).

(If favicon.svg would prove to be a popular approach, maybe the favicon.ico fallback could at some point be replaced by just a favicon.svg fallback. [I realize that’s not how this all usually works, but, maybe it‘s a prospect that makes having two fallbacks more palatable.])

**Advantages**: As described, a second vector-based fallback would greatly increase options to provision an icon format that can serve more use cases than the raster fallback we have now. With that would come a real option to curb the “icon proliferation” trend we do observe in web development, where documents are cluttered with [dozens of icons](https://realfavicongenerator.net/faq). Many of those images and their respective code would not be needed if we (literally) offered a more scalable fallback.

**Suggestion:** Pending signals to implement (and other parts of the process I’m not as familiar with yet), rephrase the section quoted above to say:

> Let _request_ be a new request whose URL is the URL record obtained by resolving the URLs "`/favicon.ico`" and "`/favicon.svg`" against the `Document` object's URL

## Appendix

### Notes

† It’s probably possible to deliver the favicon.ico as `image/svg+xml`, however this approach seems hacky and not like one we would want to promote as a best practice.

### Examples

Taken from a random website, this is quite common favicon-related markup and imagery (more on the “harmless” side of things compared to sites that offer 10+ icons and the respective markup for them):

```html
<link rel="shortcut icon" href=/favicon.ico>
<link rel=icon type=image/png sizes=16x16 href=/favicon-16x16.png>
<link rel=icon type=image/png sizes=32x32 href=/favicon-32x32.png>
<link rel=apple-touch-icon sizes=180x180 href=/apple-touch-icon-180x180.png>
<meta name=msapplication-TileImage content=/mstile-144x144.png>
```

By allowing said more scalable fallback, however, we could offer authors to work with just one file (favicon.svg) and no markup:
